focus: Compare host-side connect behavior between the live libvirt-managed qga socket and a temporary QEMU chardev socket created inside the same VM process.
findings: The live libvirt-managed qga socket path still returns ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused') on direct host-side AF_UNIX connect.

A temporary QEMU socket chardev created via QMP chardev-add at /tmp/regprobe-qga-socktest.sock accepts a direct host-side AF_UNIX connection successfully in the same running qemu-system-x86_64 process.
query-chardev shows both charchannel1 and codextest as disconnected unix socket backends with server=on.

Therefore the persistent attach failure is not a generic host-to-QEMU unix socket limitation in this VM session; it is specific to the libvirt-managed qga/virtserial channel path or its associated runtime state.
